checklist.detail: The preburner drive gas cannot power the pumps at this chamber pressure: best achievable power margin 0.91 (fuel-rich PR 1.54 @ 900 K (margin 1.01), oxidizer-rich PR 2.33 @ 628 K (margin 0.91)) with the turbine PR searched up to 3.0. A hotter preburner (preburner temperature inputs), better turbomachinery, or a lower Pc closes it - this is the staged-cycle Pc ceiling [SP-8107 Table VI].
checklist.name: Staged-combustion power balance

checklist.detail: Turbine PR 2.33 / drive-pump discharge 3.10 x Pc is outside real staged-combustion practice (PR < ~2.0, SSME 1.56-1.59; discharge ~2.1-2.3 x Pc - SSME/RD-0124/NK-33) - the turbine is being asked for an unusually large pressure drop.
checklist.name: Staged-combustion turbine PR / discharge plausibility

checklist.detail: Full-flow staged combustion uses TWO preburners (one fuel-rich, one oxidizer-rich), one per turbopump, with nearly all of both propellants gasified before the main injector - the highest plumbing/valve count and the hardest cycle to develop. Only Raptor / RD-270 / (partly) BE-4 have flown or run it.
checklist.name: FFSC development complexity

checklist.detail: GRCop-84 Copper-Chromium-Niobium Alloy: computed wall temp 1076 K EXCEEDS its 900 K max service temp (Tc 3762 K, regenerative cooling). Marginal/unsuitable as designed. Basis: coupled throat wall balance: gas h_g ~53.5 kW/m2K, T_aw ~3716 K, coolant ~73 m/s (coolant-side wall ~832 K), 0.50 mm wall. Levers that lower it: faster coolant (Coolant velocity; SP-8087 caps liquids at ~61 m/s, at a jacket-dP cost), a thinner wall, a liner rated hotter or more conductive (e.g. GRCop-84), or more film cooling.
checklist.name: Chamber material thermal margin

checklist.detail: Hottest wall station is in the convergent section (area ratio ~1.0, regen): wall ~1105 K, 0.81x that section's material limit (warns below 1.15x, like the throat row). Levers: more chamber film (or a convergent film ring for the throat region), faster coolant, a thinner or more conductive liner, or extend active cooling.
checklist.name: Peak wall temperature along the wall

checklist.detail: Throat coolant-passage velocity ~73 m/s exceeds SP-8087's 61 m/s liquid-coolant limit [SP-8087 Sec.3.1.1.5.3] - expect erosion and a steep jacket-dP / pump-power cost. Lower Coolant velocity or add film cooling instead.

checklist.detail: Resultant injection beta angle +5.6 deg is outside the -3 to +3 deg band LOX/CH4 prefers - it wants a slightly negative beta (~0 or below). Adjust the impingement angle or element momentum ratio.
checklist.name: Injector resultant beta angle

checklist.detail: First tangential mode ~2659 Hz is in the band damaging instability lives in (<4000 Hz) and the injector is soft (dP/Pc 0.15 < 0.18). Historically this regime needed an odd-compartment injector-face baffle or corner-mounted Helmholtz cavities. Stiffen the injector, or plan on damping devices.
checklist.name: Combustion acoustic-mode margin

checklist.detail: Near the end of active cooling (area ratio ~40.0), estimated jacket/coolant pressure (~36.3 MPa) exceeds local hot-gas static pressure (~0.1 MPa) - the net load on the channel-land wall there REVERSES direction. Modeled as a clamped-strip bending stress across the ~13.0 mm channel width, this reversed ~36.2 MPa differential is ~12256 MPa against a ~133 MPa allowable (Inconel 718 Nickel Superalloy, SF 1.5) - but this is a coarse clamped-plate-strip proxy, NOT a real buckling/FEA analysis, and this codebase has no real-engine spot check for it yet. Treat this as 'worth a closer structural look', not a validated failure prediction. Consider more/narrower channels (smaller span), tapering the actively-cooled length, or a thicker wall there.
checklist.name: Jacket overpressure vs. channel-wall structural margin
